claims.text: Pioglitazone 15 or 30 mg PO daily (15 mg with NYHA I–II HF);
claims.quote: Initiate ACTOS at 15 mg or 30 mg once daily. Limit initial dose to 15 mg once daily in patients with NYHA Class I or II heart failure.

claims.text: titrate by 15 mg to max 45 mg daily.
claims.quote: The dose can be titrated in increments of 15 mg up to a maximum of 45 mg once daily based on glycemic response as determined by HbA1c.

claims.text: Max 15 mg with gemfibrozil or other strong CYP2C8 inhibitors.
claims.quote: the maximum recommended dose of ACTOS is 15 mg daily when used in combination with gemfibrozil or other strong CYP2C8 inhibitors
claims.locator: 2.3 Concomitant Use with Strong CYP2C8 Inhibitors

claims.text: Boxed warning: causes or worsens CHF in some patients;
claims.quote: Thiazolidinediones, including ACTOS, cause or exacerbate congestive heart failure in some patients.
ACTOS is not recommended in patients with symptomatic heart failure.

claims.text: starting it in NYHA class III–IV HF is contraindicated.
claims.quote: Initiation of ACTOS in patients with established New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV heart failure is contraindicated

claims.text: Pioglitazone: don't use with active bladder cancer; caution with prior bladder cancer,
claims.quote: Do not use in patients with active bladder cancer. Use caution when using in patients with a prior history of bladder cancer.
ACTOS should be used with caution in patients with edema.
Use caution in patients with liver disease

claims.text: Gemfibrozil (strong CYP2C8 inhibitor) raises pioglitazone exposure about 3-fold.
claims.quote: Coadministration of ACTOS and gemfibrozil, a strong CYP2C8 inhibitor, increases pioglitazone exposure approximately 3-fold.
claims.locator: 2.3 Concomitant Use with Strong CYP2C8 Inhibitors

claims.text: With insulin, cut the insulin dose 10–25% if hypoglycemia occurs.
claims.quote: If hypoglycemia occurs in a patient co-administered ACTOS and insulin, the dose of insulin should be decreased by 10% to 25%.
claims.locator: 2.2 Concomitant Use with an Insulin Secretagogue or Insulin

claims.text: Pioglitazone: liver tests before starting; routine periodic LFTs not needed without liver disease.
claims.quote: Obtain liver tests before starting ACTOS. If abnormal, use caution when treating with ACTOS, investigate the probable cause, treat (if possible) and follow appropriately. Monitoring liver tests while on ACTOS is not recommended in patients without liver disease.

claims.text: Check LFTs promptly for symptoms of liver injury; stop if ALT > 3× ULN.
claims.quote: Measure liver tests promptly in patients who report symptoms that may indicate liver injury, including fatigue, anorexia, right upper abdominal discomfort, dark urine or jaundice. In this clinical context, if the patient is found to have abnormal liver tests (ALT greater than 3 times the upper limit of the reference range), ACTOS treatment should be interrupted

claims.text: After starting or raising the dose, watch for weight gain, edema and HF signs.
claims.quote: After initiation of ACTOS or with dose increase, monitor patients carefully for adverse reactions related to fluid retention such as weight gain, edema, and signs and symptoms of congestive heart failure
